title: The Microsegmentation portal: Application Catalog, ML tag recommendations, tags and AppZones

prose.text: The Microsegmentation pages of the Zscaler Admin Console manage the application catalog, tag recommendations, tags and AppZones. Provisioning keys are in [[zms.provisioning-keys]].

prose.label: Application Catalog.
prose.text: {{catalog-purpose}} {{catalog-filters}} The GraphQL catalog filter is narrower: [[zms.api.enums-and-filters:app-catalog-filter]].

prose.label: Tags.
prose.text: {{tag-model}} How the API walks the same hierarchy is in [[zms.api.queries:tag-hierarchy]].

checks.do: Whether the recommendation was accepted with every resource selected, since unselected resources become ignored.
Whether ML tag recommendations are enabled for the organization (Zscaler Support toggles it) and when the next check runs.

catalog-purpose.statement: The Application Catalog lists the applications and application categories that machine learning uses to recommend resource tags, which can be applied to resource groups.

quotes: The Application Catalog gives admins insight into the applications used to generate the machine-learning (ML) tags that you can apply to resource groups.
Review the list of applications and application categories used by ML to recommend resource tags.

catalog-filters.statement: The Application Catalog page filters by Application Name, Application Category, Process, Protocol and Port, and lists for each application its name, category, process name, protocol, and port start and end.

quotes: Filter the information by Application Name, Application Category, Process, Protocol, and Port.
Application Name: The name of the application.
Application Category: The type of application.
Process Name: The name of the process file.
Protocol: The protocol type (UDP, TCP, etc.).
Port Start: The port starting number.
Port End: The port ending number.

ml-recommendations.statement: The ML Tag Recommendations page shows which Application Catalog applications were detected running on managed resources; a recommendation can be reviewed and accepted, edited, ignored or deleted, and resources left unselected when accepting are treated as ignored.

quotes: The machine learning (ML) Tag Recommendations page shows which applications from the Applications Catalog have been detected running on managed resources in the environment.
Review a recommendation to view its complete information and accept, edit, or ignore it. Any resources that are not selected while accepting the recommendation are considered ignored.
Delete a recommendation.

ml-ignored-list.statement: Previously ignored recommendations are reviewed from a separate ignored list.

quotes: If the user wants to review the previously ignored recommendations, they must check that list.
Show or hide the ignored list of ML tag recommendations.

ml-schedule.statement: The page shows when a recommendations check last ran and when the next is scheduled, and Zscaler Support enables or disables ML tag recommendations for an organization.

quotes: View the last time a recommendations check was run, and when the next check is scheduled.
View instructions to have Zscaler Support enable or disable ML tag recommendations for your organization.

tag-model.statement: Tags are configured as namespaces, keys and values; a fully configured tag can be assigned to resource groups, and the Tag Management page adds namespaces and tags and edits and deletes tags.

quotes: The Tag Management page allows you to configure tag data, such as namespaces, keys, and values. After a tag is fully configured with those data components, you can assign the tag to resource groups.
Add a namespace.
Add a tag.
Edit a tag.
Delete a tag.

app-zones.statement: AppZones group applications into zones based on the applications' topology and their network connectivity with each other; the AppZones page adds, edits and deletes AppZones and lists each one's name, member count (resources connected to it) and description.

quotes: AppZones in Microsegmentation are applications grouped together into zones based on the applications' topology and their underlying network connectivity with each other.
Name: The name of the AppZone.
Member Count: The number of resources connected to the AppZone.
Description: Contextual information about the AppZone.
Add an AppZone.
Edit an AppZone.
Delete an AppZone.

portal-no-contract.statement: The portal's write actions (accepting, editing, ignoring or deleting recommendations; adding, editing and deleting namespaces, tags and AppZones) have no published programmatic operation: the captured pages describe only the UI, and the Python SDK and MCP clients implement reads only.
portal-no-contract.conditions: Rests on reading the five captured portal pages, which describe UI actions with no API operation, enum or payload, and on zms.api:clients-read-only.
